explanation: The request cannot ship with the ordered tier's contract. In the observed run (incident 4712, destination dst-4f2a) the consumer's ingest log shows evt-2f9c-0003 through evt-2f9c-0008 acknowledged while evt-2f9c-0002, the event their endpoint was rejecting, was still undelivered — and 0002 only landed after recovery, behind everything accepted after it. Delivering a later event before an earlier one is acknowledged is precisely what the contract's order property forbids, so 'keep delivering later events while the head fails' is not a relaxation of ordering, it is the loss of it. Batching cannot rescue it either: the receiver answers a whole request at once, so a request containing the failing event fails as a unit, and widening delivery_batch_size only puts more events behind the same blocked head. The only way to obtain the requested progress is to remove the rejected events from the stream (or re-add them behind later work), which is what the service was doing before the fix: the head's original stream record was deleted and a copy took its place at the back of the group, which is exactly how 0002 came to arrive last. The ordered tier's choice is therefore to hold the destination: at most one delivery in flight, the rejected head retained on the stream under its original identity, retried until the destination recovers, and later events delivered after it. Availability during a consumer failure is a different tier, not a mode of this one.
